interest: Contrasts 1940 praise for Japanese state monopolies as anti-Communist with 1944 U.S. planning on postwar Zaibatsu deconcentration.
overview: File 894.602 (1940-44): attorney Monningh proposes 'Industrial Monocracy,' citing Japanese monopolies in Manchoukuo and China as anti-Communist models, acknowledged by Hamilton; a 1944 Lockhart memo to Remer assesses extending Roosevelt's anti-cartel policy to Japan's Zaibatsu, weighing occupation controls against long-term multilateral trade goals.

subfiles.about: Letter from C. P. Monningh to Secretary of State Cordell Hull presenting his interpretation of Japanese monopolies in Manchoukuo and China as a strategy against Communism.
subfiles.summary: Monningh tells Hull Japan's monopolies in Manchoukuo and occupied China counter Communism, citing War Minister Hata's rice monopoly, and requests information while enclosing his own 'Industrial Monocracy' reform proposal.
subfiles.title: Letter from C. P. Monningh to Secretary of State Cordell Hull on Japanese Monopolies

subfiles.about: An enclosed theoretical synopsis outlining 'Industrial Monocracy', an economic system aimed at eliminating commercial competition through planned national monopolies.
subfiles.summary: Monningh's enclosure proposes worldwide 'Industrial Monocracy': merchants trade patents and assets for shares in national monopoly corporations, eliminating competition, poverty, and anti-trust law via industrial balancing and martial law.
subfiles.title: Synopsis of 'Industrial Monocarcy' by C. P. Monningh

subfiles.about: Formal acknowledgment from the Department of State to C. P. Monningh regarding his letter and enclosed article on 'Industrial Monosracy'.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton acknowledges Monningh's February 1940 letter and 'Industrial Monosracy' article on behalf of Hull, thanking him for his civic-minded economic proposal.
subfiles.title: Letter from Maxwell M. Hamilton to C. P. Monningh Acknowledging Letter on 'Industrial Monosracy'

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum by Frank P. Lockhart evaluating Rudolph's prospectus on the post-war Japanese cartel system and long-range economic policy.
subfiles.summary: Lockhart tells Remer that Roosevelt's German-cartel policy applies to Japan's Zaibatsu, but warns short-term military occupation measures may conflict with long-term economic policy, questioning Rudolph's plan to integrate Japan into multilateral trade.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Frank P. Lockhart to Charles F. Remer on Japanese Cartel System Prospectus
